messages.text: How do changes in automotive radar technology affect the measurement capability required from Vector Network Analyzer?

Short answer: As the cited automotive-radar test setup moves toward wider IF bandwidth, more digital channels/objects, near-object capability, Doppler extension, and time-domain ghost-object checks, the VNA needs wider frequency-span coverage, time-domain analysis, fine frequency stepping, low measurement bandwidth options, adequate dynamic range, and possibly mmWave RF coverage rather than only low-GHz IF capability [1][2][3][13].
The AREG800A production configurations include a one-channel mini configuration with one object per channel, 5 GHz instantaneous bandwidth, near-object range possibility, analog IF output interfaces, and frontend options [3].
The same production family also includes two-digital-channel and three-digital-channel configurations, with the pro configuration supporting monostatic or bistatic frontends and one object per channel [3].
The listed technology/options include baseband extension from 1 GHz to 2 GHz IF bandwidth, extension from 2 GHz to 5 GHz IF bandwidth, activation of a second IF path, one additional artificial object, extended Doppler frequency shift up to 10 MHz, and near-object range for FMCW [13].
For IF transfer-characteristic measurement, the VNA conditions are frequency step size 2.5 MHz, measurement bandwidth 1 kHz, source power –10 dBm, and spans of 1.1 GHz to 2.1 GHz, 0.7 GHz to 2.7 GHz, or 0.7 GHz to 5.7 GHz depending on bandwidth [2].
For ghost-object suppression, the measurement condition explicitly uses a vector network analyzer in time domain, with 125 kHz frequency step size, 100 kHz measurement bandwidth, –10 dBm source power, 2 m wanted-artificial-object distance, and spans up to 0.7 GHz to 5.7 GHz [1].
The echo-generator dynamic RCS range is 90 dB for all artificial objects on one IF path with AREG8-24S/24D/81S/81D, 60 dB for multiple objects per IF path with those same frontends, and the RCS control step size is 0.1 dB [2].
ZNB3020 system dynamic range is specified as at least 140 dB from 100 MHz to 24 GHz and at least 135 dB from 24 GHz to 26.5 GHz at 10 Hz measurement bandwidth [24].
ZNA67 covers 10 MHz to 67 GHz, has 1 Hz frequency resolution, up to 100001 points, and measurement bandwidth from 1 Hz to 1.5 MHz or up to 30 MHz with the increased IF bandwidth option [52].
ZNA67EXT covers 10 MHz to 110 GHz, uses 1.0 mm test ports, has 1 Hz frequency resolution, up to 100001 points, and measurement bandwidths from 1 Hz to 1.5 MHz [34][38].
【推論】Because the radar echo-generator options extend IF bandwidth from 1 GHz to 5 GHz and the VNA IF measurement spans extend up to 0.7 GHz to 5.7 GHz, wider-band automotive-radar evolution pushes the VNA requirement from narrow IF spans toward multi-GHz IF span coverage [13][2].
【推論】Because production configurations add more digital channels and options add a second IF path and additional artificial object, VNA measurement workflows need to support repeated characterization across more paths/objects, although the passages specify measurement conditions rather than throughput requirements [3][13][2].

Short answer: As the cited automotive-radar test setup moves toward wider IF bandwidth, more digital channels/objects, near-object capability, Doppler extension, and time-domain ghost-object checks, the VNA needs wider frequency-span coverage, time-domain analysis, fine frequency stepping, low measurement bandwidth options, adequate dynamic range, and possibly mmWave RF coverage rather than only low-GHz IF capability [1][2][3][13].
The AREG800A production configurations include a one-channel mini configuration with one object per channel, 5 GHz instantaneous bandwidth, near-object range possibility, analog IF output interfaces, and frontend options [3].
The same production family also includes two-digital-channel and three-digital-channel configurations, with the pro configuration supporting monostatic or bistatic frontends and one object per channel [3].
The listed technology/options include baseband extension from 1 GHz to 2 GHz IF bandwidth, extension from 2 GHz to 5 GHz IF bandwidth, activation of a second IF path, one additional artificial object, extended Doppler frequency shift up to 10 MHz, and near-object range for FMCW [13].
For IF transfer-characteristic measurement, the VNA conditions are frequency step size 2.5 MHz, measurement bandwidth 1 kHz, source power –10 dBm, and spans of 1.1 GHz to 2.1 GHz, 0.7 GHz to 2.7 GHz, or 0.7 GHz to 5.7 GHz depending on bandwidth [2].
For ghost-object suppression, the measurement condition explicitly uses a vector network analyzer in time domain, with 125 kHz frequency step size, 100 kHz measurement bandwidth, –10 dBm source power, 2 m wanted-artificial-object distance, and spans up to 0.7 GHz to 5.7 GHz [1].
The echo-generator dynamic RCS range is 90 dB for all artificial objects on one IF path with AREG8-24S/24D/81S/81D, 60 dB for multiple objects per IF path with those same frontends, and the RCS control step size is 0.1 dB [2].
ZNB3020 system dynamic range is specified as at least 140 dB from 100 MHz to 24 GHz and at least 135 dB from 24 GHz to 26.5 GHz at 10 Hz measurement bandwidth [24].
ZNA67 covers 10 MHz to 67 GHz, has 1 Hz frequency resolution, up to 100001 points, and measurement bandwidth from 1 Hz to 1.5 MHz or up to 30 MHz with the increased IF bandwidth option [52].
ZNA67EXT covers 10 MHz to 110 GHz, uses 1.0 mm test ports, has 1 Hz frequency resolution, up to 100001 points, and measurement bandwidths from 1 Hz to 1.5 MHz [34][38].
【推論】Because the radar echo-generator options extend IF bandwidth from 1 GHz to 5 GHz and the VNA IF measurement spans extend up to 0.7 GHz to 5.7 GHz, wider-band automotive-radar evolution pushes the VNA requirement from narrow IF spans toward multi-GHz IF span coverage [13][2].
【推論】Because production configurations add more digital channels and options add a second IF path and additional artificial object, VNA measurement workflows need to support repeated characterization across more paths/objects, although the passages specify measurement conditions rather than throughput requirements [3][13][2].
